The Winterpelt Furbolg are a very isolated furbolg tribe based out of Winterpelt Hollow in northeastern Azure Span on the Dragon Isles. The Winterpelt were unique amongst the furbolg tribes of the Dragon Isles due to their isolationist nature. After the Primalists arrived in the Azure Span, they sought to recruit the furbolg tribes of the span into their forces. While the Rustpine clan accepted this bargain and joined the Primalists, the Winterpelt refused and subsequently found themselves enslaved by Stormshackler Rynea. The lieutenants of their group, the Witchwing Slayers, are a nasty bunch, but they lead some of the underlings in that area. They stand out from the rest by wearing some rings. WoWSearch is a World of Warcraft meta-search engine. The site has only one page that allows you to use main search engines to search game database, addons, and The Armory. You can also perform multiple search dividing the subject of your search with the ";" character. WoWSearch provides 1 tool: WoWSwitch creates a special Bookmark in your Bookmarks bar that allows you to search the same thing in different website. How does it work? It's simple! You're look for something in Thottbot but there are no comments? You landed in an empty Wowpedia page? Use the bookmark to find the same thing in another search engine! Works with Thottbot, Allakhazam, Wowhead, Wowpedia and The Armory.

[http://www.WoWScan.com WoWScan.com] is a really awesome website/tool for pet, mount -and recipe collectors. The website lists the cheapest items on every server with a single click on the search button. This is especially useful to (TCG) collectors who are willing to transfer to another server to get some of the cheapest deals possible. It's of course also useful as a price guide for items, as it gives you a quick idea of how much an item is worth. They're planning to expand the website to include every in-game item possible, but for now they've launched with pets, mounts and recipes only. Their website is 100% legit and free to use, no user accounts are required! ---- WoW Scan FAQ

WoWWiki was the original name of Wowpedia during its launch on 24 November 2004. In 2007 the wiki joined and transferred legal rights for the "wowwiki.com" domain. Three years later, Wikia implemented visual interface changes across its platform that broke some of WoWWiki's functionality and was poorly received by some of WoWWiki's community. As a result, a cohort of non-employee admins and active users decided to leave Wikia and forked the wiki project to Wowpedia in October 2010. In May 2020, the decision was made to close WoWWiki and encourage its users to migrate to Wowpedia.

A wizard's desk travels folded up to the size of a small trunk. When the legs are extended, the side can fold down to become a writing surface. Inside are compartments for material components, spellbooks, parchment, inks... and the tinker-created device that makes wizard's desks so sought after. From one side of the interior, an articulated arm can be unfolded. At its tip is a stylus with a tube that runs back down the arm and is connected to a vial of ink. Stabilized by springs and providing an uninterrupted flow of ink, this design allows spellcasters to work quickly and precisely when scribing scrolls.

WoW Insider, formerly known as WoW.com, was a popular blog and news site about World of Warcraft that occasionally referenced Wowpedia. The site was launched on November 23, 2005 with just a small team of bloggers but grew to be one of the leading WoW-related websites. Besides covering WoW news, the site featured a number of columns on various topics such as character classes, add-ons, and Warcraft lore. Each column generally has one blogger with the exception of the class columns, which may have different bloggers for each specialization the class offers. Wooly Kodo are kodo that grow much longer hair than the ordinary breed. They can be found in the Barrens.

Wood Mite can be found in Terokkar Forest. When a treant is slain in the area while you have the quest The Infested Protectors, these wood mites will exit and attack those responsible. There are 5 wood mites per tree, despite them being aggressive they have low accuracy on hits and only deal 1 damage.
The Wooden Key drops from Crazed Ancients and Withered Ancients in Ashenvale.

.]] Wolpertingers are small hare-like critters who have the head, body, feet, and tail of a hare with bird wings, antlers, and fangs. They only appear during Brewfest, as they are attracted to the scents of the festival, and can only be seen by drunk characters. Many a drunken Brewfest goer has told the tale of this mysterious creature, but few remember that tale in the morning. A drunk hunter can track them using beast tracking.
Wolpertinger's Tankard summons and dismisses a Wolpertinger, a wolpertinger battle pet.
Word of Thawing is an item used to unlock Frozen Runes in Naxxramas.
Wolf Handler Gloves are a quest reward from Dwarven Outfitters.

The wolverine guardian is an unnamed Ancient Guardian that fought during the War of the Ancients. Slightly smaller than Ursoc and Ursol, this Ancient resembled a wolverine with six limbs and a serpentine tail, who eagerly surveyed the distant battlefield. His breath came in hungry pants and his massive claws raked the ground, creating massive grooves. He was the first of the demigods to fall.
The Woodpaw Battle Map is located in one of the gnoll's camps in Woodpaw Hills of Feralas.
The Wooden Outhouse is located in Grimesilt Dig Site of Searing Gorge. Locked inside is Locheed.

Wooly Rhino Calves are rhinos found in the Borean Tundra. They spawn in groups containing 4 calves, matriarch and bull.

The Wolfcult is a mysterious organization that is predominantly found in the Grizzly Hills of southern Northrend and is primarily made up of the region's local human trappers. It is led by none other than the Shade of Archmage Arugal, who had previously adopted the worgen of Silverpine Forest in northern Lordaeron as his children and was once a part of the unrelated Wolf Cult.

The Woodpaw clan of gnolls is native to Feralas. They have been seen as a danger to both the night elves and tauren in the forest, and adventurers are often sent to combat the menace. These gnolls can be found in northeastern and southeastern Feralas. They were led by their alphas as well as a matriarch.
Wolf Droppings can be found throughout the western part of the Geyser Fields in the Borean Tundra.
The Wonderworks (also known as the Wonderworks Toy Shop) is a toy store found in Dalaran.

Wooly Mammoth is a collections achievement earned for obtaining a Reins of the Wooly Mammoth/ Reins of the Wooly Mammoth#Horde mount from for in Dalaran.
The Wolvar Orphan Whistle is provided by Orphan Matron Aria for players who accept the quest Little Orphan Kekek Of The Wolvar for Children's Week. It can summon Kekek.
Wodin's Lucky Necklace drops from trash mobs in Icecrown Citadel.
Wooly Stompers are a reward for completing Valkyrion Must Burn.

Wolf's Run is a path that leads from the Verdant Thicket to the Shrine of Goldrinn and Shrine of Aviana in Mount Hyjal. The path after the Shrine of Aviana has been consumed and altered by the Twilight's Hammer and is known as the Lightning Ledge. The Twilight's Hammer is using ogres, to protect and prevent Twilight Slaves from running, to transport supplies to the Twilight Command Post. Oomla Whitehorn and Jadi Falaryn are quest givers found at the beginning of the path near the Verdant Thicket.

WoWphiles was a non-official WoW fansite which provides World of Warcraft players with a Blog and Podcast that is focused on entertaining and informing. Wolf Tender's Boots are a quest reward from Through Fire and Flames.

World of Warcraft: Wolfheart is a novel by Richard A. Knaak. New York Times bestselling author Richard A. Knaak's latest book chronicles a series of pivotal events in the aftermath of the Cataclysm, as conflict engulfs every corner of Azeroth. Hungering for more resources amid the turmoil, the Horde have pressed into Ashenvale to feed their burgeoning war machine. There, acting warchief Garrosh Hellscream has employed a brutal new tactic to conquer the region and crush its night elf defenders. Unless the Alliance can overcome its own political strife, the new warchief might succeed in seizing Ashenvale. __NOTOC__ Woodpaw Alphas are gnoll leaders of the Woodpaw tribe found at the Woodpaw Den in Feralas.

[http://wowlazymacros.com WoW Lazy Macros] is a blog site dedicated to lazy macros and normal macros in World of Warcraft. It provides continuous updates to their macros for every current patch. Their macro list contains all specs for all classes related to damage (tank,dps). The author of this site also created a plugin addOn for MacroBank add-on called "[http://wow.curse.com/downloads/wow-addons/details/wowlazymacros-plugin-macrobank.aspx WoWLazyMacros Plugin for MacroBank]" that imports all the lazy macros provided in the site to the game. He also created a community site for the upcoming pet battle system named WoW Pet Battles.

Wolfmaw Outriders are the mounted units the Horde have brought in their attempt to drive back the worgen and their allies from the Headlands in Gilneas. They often ride in packs of four or more, usually closest to the center of the area. They ride on Riding War Wolves.

[http://wowpetbattles.com WoW Pet Battles] is a blog/fan community site dedicated to the new upcoming Pet Battle System in World of Warcraft: Mists of Pandaria. It provides news, tips and forum discussions related to the companion pets in-game. They also have giveaways every few weeks to help you build a team with the in-game pets from the Loot Cards. The author of this site also created a blog dedicated to lazy macros.
Wolfcult Initiates are found at Solstice Village in the Grizzly Hills. They transform into worgen when their health gets low.
Wobbling Raptor Egg are found among clutches that the raptors have laid under the trees in Saltspray Glen in the Wetlands.

The Wood of Staves is a grove found to the far west on the Wandering Isle, that only the worthy pandaren are allowed to enter. This is determined by proving oneself worthy to the Guardian of the Elders. A cruel breed of forest sprite lives here. This grove is the final resting place for pandaren elders, beginning with Liu Lang, the first explorer to leave Pandaria. He likely traveled to that particular spot because it also happens to be the closest point of the land where one can be near and see the head of Shen-zin Su. The Woods of the Lost is a wooded area in northeastern Jade Forest between Emperor's Omen and the Terrace of Ten Thunders. Ancient mogu statues have entered the area from the terrace and have started killing forest sprites.
Woolly Sheep are sheep found in Thunderfoot Fields in the Valley of the Four Winds. They are terrorized by Thieving Wolves and Thieving Plainshawks.
Wooden Spoon is a grummle found in front of Shado-Pan Monastery in Kun-Lai Summit.
Woodcarver Liupo is a pandaren vendor located at Greenstone Village in Jade Forest.
Wolf Piranhas are fished up from the Krasarang River in Krasarang Wilds while on the Anglers daily quest Piranha!.

Wodin's Mantid Shanker can be found at Owen's Wishing Well at the north coast of Jade Forest and is one of the treasures of Pandaria. The weapon is Bind to Account and is One-Hand equip, plus it allows for use in transmogrification.
